e-12694.knowledge_point: Negating a Sentence Containing a Conjunction
e-12694.problem:
What is the negation of the following compound statement? 

$\qquad$ $6$ is composite and $5\!\not{|} \, 3.$
e-12694.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
\neg ( A \land B) = \neg A \lor \neg B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(6\text{ is composite}\text{ and }5\,\text{⧸}|\,3) & ≡¬((6\text{ is composite})∧(5\,\text{⧸}|\,3)) \\  & ≡¬(6\text{ is composite})∨¬(5\,\text{⧸}|\,3) \\  & ≡(6\text{ is not composite})∨(5\,|\,3) \\  & ≡6\text{ is not composite}\text{ or }5\,|\,3.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$\,$ $0\le 2$ and $4.3$ is not irrational

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
after.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(0\le 2\text{ and }4.3\text{ is not irrational}) & ≡¬((0\le 2)∧(4.3\text{ is not irrational})) \\  & ≡¬(0\le 2)∨¬(4.3\text{ is not irrational}) \\  & ≡(0>2)∨(4.3\text{ is irrational}) \\  & ≡(0>2)\text{ or }4.3\text{ is irrational}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$\,$ $|{1,x}|\ne 0$ and $x$ is rational

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
after.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(|{1,x}|\ne 0\text{ and }x\text{ is rational}) & ≡¬((|{1,x}|\ne 0)∧(x\text{ is rational})) \\  & ≡¬(|{1,x}|\ne 0)∨¬(x\text{ is rational}) \\  & ≡(|{1,x}|=0)∨(x\text{ is not rational}) \\  & ≡|{1,x}|=0\text{ or }x\text{ is not rational}.\end{aligned}
$$
